changes.before: Are Party D's priced proposals from 04/15/2021 Formal (with Heavy conditions)? The support is D's Merger Agreement markup of 04/08, revised 04/27, and its 05/13 markups of the signed Gray agreements.
changes.after: Are D’s structure and commitment revisions from April 13 onward Formal with Heavy conditions?

changes.before: E11(1): markups of the acquisition agreement supported the priced proposals (pp.65, 69, 72). They were subject to diligence, structure and financing, and firm financing was missing, hence Heavy. The 05/13 and 05/26 letters call themselves 'non-binding', which does not decide formality.
changes.after: April 8 acquisition markup supports April 13 and later proposals; April 27 adds material closing/recourse terms (pp.65–69). May 13 markups support later proposals (p.72). Diligence, structure and uncommitted financing remain Heavy; non-binding wording does not decide formality.

changes.before: Informal would show D as a weaker, conditional rival to Gray in round 3 and after signing. It affects whether the final stage had more than one formal bidder.
changes.after: Informal would show D as a less formal rival in round 4 and after signing, changing whether the final stage had multiple formal bidders.

changes.before: Should Party D's Reverse Morris Trust / Morris Trust proposals (cash for debt refinancing and a dividend, plus 50.7%, later down to 10%, of a combined company) be whole-company Bids with All cash = No?
changes.after: Should Bid versus Other-scope bid use pre-separation economic Meredith or all shares of LMG RemainCo?

changes.before: Yes. Each was a proposal 'to acquire LMG' or LMG RemainCo, the business Gray bought, and the board compared them directly with Gray's bids.
changes.after: Prefer economic pre-separation scope and Other-scope bid for LMG proposals. Retain provisional Bid labels until Alex confirms that dataset convention. Exclusion from structural estimation is already settled; descriptive/reduced-form use remains.

changes.before: pp.63–74: the filing calls them proposals to acquire LMG and LMG RemainCo. From 04/13/2021 they spun off NMG exactly as the Gray deal does. The 03/11 version spun off LMG instead, but the whole LMG business still passed to the combined company.
changes.after: NMG is spun off and only LMG passes to Gray (pp.59–60); D’s structures also concern LMG. Alex’s voice notes identify partial economic scope and lack of unaffected LMG market price. Legal acquisition of all residual-company shares does not settle dataset scope.

changes.before: Treating D's proposals, or only the 03/11 RMT, as Other-scope bids would remove D's whole-company bids from rounds 2–3 and post. That would leave Gray almost unopposed in the final stage.
changes.after: All 26 LMG proposal rows would change Bid to Other-scope bid, retaining their prices, dates and terms. Together with 10 station rows this gives 36 Other-scope bids. Do not reopen the settled structural-estimation exclusion.

changes.before: LMG bids are stated as enterprise values, EV ranges, or (for Party D) cash plus a stake in a new combined company. Per-share figures appear only from signing onward. Should price cells stay blank where no per-share total is given, including D's implied per-share cash dividends?
changes.after: How should EV, cash-plus-equity packages and cash dividends be represented without treating unlike values as comparable whole-offer prices?

changes.before: Yes. Keep EV and structure in the Notes. Fill price cells only for Gray's stated per-share offers ($15.25, $16.99, $16.55). Leave D's cash-only figures ($15.71, $14.99, $16.51) out of the price cells.
changes.after: Keep EV/package values in Notes. Use stated whole-offer per-share amounts only, including Gray’s $14.51 first agreed May 1–2. D’s cash dividends exclude equity and remain in Notes.

changes.before: E13 fills per-share cells only with a per-share figure for the whole offer. D's figures are cash dividends and exclude its stake in the combined company (pp.71, 74). EVs could be turned into per-share values only through the $1.975B net-debt figure agreed on 05/02/2021 (p.70), which the filing does not apply to earlier bids.
changes.after: E13: Gray’s $1.975B net debt allocation first fixes $725M/$14.51 shareholder cash May 1–2 (p.70); do not back-apply it to earlier EV bids. D’s dividends omit retained equity (pp.71,74).

changes.before: Converting EVs would add per-share prices to most pre-signing bids. Entering D's cash figures as prices would understate D's offers, which also included 10–50.8% of the combined company.
changes.after: Converting earlier EVs would invent comparable per-share prices; using D’s dividend alone would omit the equity component.

changes.after: A/C/D: inferred Dropped by target at the January 28 pause, Not stated reasons. D re-enters March 11. B: inferred target exclusion by April 23, Not stated reason; no reported call or withdrawal.

changes.before: p.61: A was invited to bid for LMG, but only two LMG proposals came in, and the 01/28 update names only Gray's and B's (p.62). The pause left station-only bidders without a stage (p.62). D came back uninvited (p.63).
changes.after: A’s station offer remains outstanding January 25–26, so missing an LMG proposal does not close participation early. Station track pauses January 28 (pp.61–62); D returns uninvited (p.63). Board continues Gray/D and authorizes communicating uncompetitiveness to B, without reporting the call (p.68).

changes.before: Alternatives: A as Dropped by target at the pause (its station bid was still outstanding), or D kept live throughout (no exit or re-entry). Either would change the live count between 01/28 and 03/11/2021 and whether A's exit signals its valuation.
changes.after: Keeping D continuously live removes its exit/re-entry. Keeping B live until signing changes late participation counts. Do not interpret target comparisons as the bidder’s own valuation.

changes.before: E5 tests: (a) no; Gray and B stayed in LMG diligence (p.63) and D returned 03/11/2021. (b) No break: no gap of about two months without acquirer contact between 11/16/2020 and 06/02/2021. (c) Not needed. Gaps of about two months or more: Fall 2019–11/16/2020 (before the process) and 06/02/2021–10/06/2021 (after signing; Gray's consent to Dotdash). Next-best alternative: open a round at the 01/28/2021 pivot, since Feb 2021 was an LMG diligence stage (pp.62–63). R2's Finality reflects the station offers called 'final'; the LMG proposals in R2 were preliminary.
changes.after: December advancement and January 12 first-final request are distinct (pp.60–61). Gray/B continue LMG diligence (pp.62–63), so E5 does not establish a process break. Fall 2019–November 2020 predates the organized process; June 2–October 6 follows signing.

changes.before: Split at 01/28/2021: rows #37–#43 would form a new round 3, and #44–#68 would become round 4. Dating R2 from 01/12/2021 would move #23 to 01/12/2021 and put #24 in round 1. Live-bidder counts at each opening would be unchanged.

changes.record_label: Deal fact Currency and units of bid prices
changes.before: US dollars. LMG bids before signing are stated as enterprise values or EV ranges ($ billions). Party D's bids are cash consideration plus a percentage of a new combined company, with implied cash dividends per share given from 04/29/2021. Per-share cash prices appear only from signing ($14.51) and in Gray's post-signing offers. Station bids are aggregate dollar amounts. Mixed bases: see Q4.
changes.after: US dollars. Station proposals use aggregate millions; LMG proposals generally use enterprise values in billions. Party D combines cash for debt refinancing/dividends with equity in a new company; its per-share dividends exclude that equity. Gray’s $14.51/share cash was agreed May 1–2 before signing. Mixed bases: Q4.

changes.before: Meredith Corporation (NYSE: MDP). What is sold is Meredith holding only its local media group (LMG, 17 TV stations), after spinning off its national media group (NMG) as NMG SpinCo.
changes.after: Meredith Corporation (NYSE: MDP), containing NMG and LMG before separation. This process offers selected stations and then LMG; Gray acquires the surviving Meredith legal entity holding LMG after NMG is spun off.

changes.before: Meredith first tried to sell four TV stations, and Moelis contacted 20 parties from 11/16/2020, of which 17 signed NDAs. Gray, Party A and Party B also indicated interest in buying all of the LMG station group after a spin-off of NMG. After final station bids in January 2021, the board paused the station sale and ran a final LMG round with Gray and Party B from 03/17/2021, while Party D pressed uninvited Morris Trust proposals. The board judged Gray strongest on 04/23/2021, dropped Party B and signed with Gray on 05/03/2021 at EV $2.7B ($14.51 per share cash plus NMG SpinCo shares). Party D's post-signing proposals led Gray to raise its price through an amendment signed 06/02/2021, at $16.99 per share with a $113M break fee.
changes.after: Meredith offered four stations through outreach starting November 16, 2020; 20 parties contacted, 17 NDAs. December advancement into diligence preceded final station offers requested January 12, 2021, while Gray/B pursued LMG. Board paused stations January 28; final LMG solicitation March 17 included D’s cash/equity alternative. Gray preferred April 23; May 1–2 debt allocation fixed $14.51 before May 3 signing/announcement. D’s post-signing bids led to June 2 amendment at $16.99. Alex excluded structural estimation because acquired LMG has no unaffected market price; retain for descriptive/reduced-form use.

changes.before: Yes. Proposals for LMG RemainCo (Meredith after the NMG spin-off) are treated as whole-company bids. Bids for the four select stations (Nov 2020–Jan 2021) are Other-scope.
changes.after: Yes under the provisional legal-entity convention: proposals for LMG RemainCo are coded Bid. Economically they acquire LMG after separation of NMG, not pre-separation Meredith including both businesses. Coding remains for Alex under Q7. Meredith is excluded from structural estimation and retained for descriptive/reduced-form use.
